title: Simultaneous inference of environmental and interaction forces in collective dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2608.25181v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Collective dynamics arise in a wide range of physical, biological, and engineering applications. Examples include cell migration, swarm robotics, social dynamics, and animal behavior. A defining characteristic of these systems is the emergence of large-scale coordination from local interactions among agents; a fundamental question is thus to understand the local interactions that give rise to the observed emergent dynamics. We are interested in methods for learning interactions generally, which can describe a wide class of physical systems exhibiting collective dynamics defined by an interaction kernel, without a priori assumptions on the analytical form of this kernel (i.e. it is nonparametric). The advantage of this kernel-based approach is that it incorporates the underlying physics of the model (i.e. collective dynamics), which more general equation-learning approaches may ignore, potentially limiting their effectiveness for model ac

translated_title: 集体动力学中环境力与相互作用力的联合推断
translated_abstract: 集体动力学广泛出现在物理、生物和工程应用中，例如细胞迁移、群体机器人、社会动态和动物行为。这些系统的一个显著特征是从个体间的局部相互作用中涌现出大规模协调；因此，一个基本问题是理解导致观察到的涌现动态的局部相互作用。我们关注于学习相互作用的一般方法，这些方法能够描述由相互作用核定义的一类广泛的集体动力学物理系统，而无需对该核的解析形式进行先验假设（即非参数方法）。这种基于核的方法的优势在于它融入了模型的底层物理（即集体动力学），而更通用的方程学习方法可能忽略这一点，从而可能限制其在模型精确性方面的有效性。
tldr: 本文提出了一种非参数核学习方法，用于同时推断集体动力学中的环境力和相互作用力，无需对核函数形式做先验假设，从而更准确地捕捉底层物理机制。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a nonparametric kernel-based method to simultaneously infer environmental and interaction forces in collective dynamics, without prior assumptions on the kernel form, thereby better capturing the underlying physics.
